LESSON: SINGING GAMES

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Singing Games

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Singing Games. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which songs do you learner should be able to:- variety of live or recorded singing sing during play?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform various singing games from the locality using ICT 2. Name some of the games drawn from the local devices. materials or objects culture for enjoyment, used during play. •
2. practice game etiquette for etiquette and share available own and others respect, resources equitably during
3. share available resources performance of singing games. during performance of • In groups and individually
4. appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SINGING GAMES
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Singing Games helps you succeed in MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SINGING GAMES
Study Singing Games like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Perform various singing games from the locality using ICT 2. Name some of the games drawn from the local devices. materials or objects culture for enjoyment, used during play. •

What this means
In this part you learn to perform various singing games from the locality using ICT 2. Name some of the games drawn from the local devices. materials or objects culture for enjoyment, used during play. •. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform various singing games from the locality using ICT 2. Name some of the games drawn from the local devices. materials or objects culture for enjoyment, used during play. •.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Singing Games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform various singing games from the locality using ICT 2. Name some of the games drawn from the local devices. materials or objects culture for enjoyment, used during play. •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE.

3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Singing Games is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Singing Games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform various singing games from the locality using ICT 2. Name some of the games drawn from the local devices. materials or objects culture for enjoyment, used during play. •)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Singing Games in your own words. (skill: practice game etiquette for etiquette and share available own and others respect, resources equitably during)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: share available resources performance of singing games. during performance of • In groups and individually)

Example 4: Show how “Singing Games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Singing Games to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: perform various singing games from the locality using ICT 2. Name some of the games drawn from the local devices. materials or objects culture for enjoyment, used during play. •.
3. Practise this skill: practice game etiquette for etiquette and share available own and others respect, resources equitably during.
4. Practise this skill: share available resources performance of singing games. during performance of • In groups and individually.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Singing Games from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Singing Games: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Singing Games?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which songs do you learner should be able to:- variety of live or recorded singing sing during play?
2. What roles do you like singing games with game aspects, singing, movement, props taking during play?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Singing Games means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: perform various singing games from the locality using ICT 2. Name some of the games drawn from the local devices. materials or objects culture for enjoyment, used during play. •.
5. Be able to: practice game etiquette for etiquette and share available own and others respect, resources equitably during.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
